scope: Narrow tests-first correction to D6-A: a ball in AIRBORNE must not be isolated from a simultaneously active CLOTH_SUPPORTED, RAIL_TOP_SUPPORTED, or OUTSIDE_LANDING_SUPPORTED ball. It adds no D6-B telemetry, D6-C classification, rules, product, UI, renderer, GPU, readiness, capture, threshold, camera, layout, asset, or product-exposure authority.

root_pm_decision.reason: The parent gate requires all 3D candidates on a temporary GameState, absolute whole-tick TOI ordering, and existing rigid-contact conventions; a split solver may not silently ignore an airborne-to-supported ball contact.

continuous_candidate_contract.candidate_pair: canonical min/max ball identity plus both physical-domain analytic segment identities
continuous_candidate_contract.geometry: continuous swept sphere versus swept sphere using center distance equal to the sum of radii
continuous_candidate_contract.time_basis: absolute whole-tick seconds; recursive tails retain the original tick origin
continuous_candidate_contract.motion_inputs: the exact analytic position, velocity, and acceleration law active for each domain segment; no endpoint chord or final-overlap proxy
continuous_candidate_contract.root_selection: earliest finite root in the closed segment interval whose approach derivative is strictly negative, within the existing solver TOI tolerance
continuous_candidate_contract.candidate_order: absolute whole-tick TOI, then existing physical feature order, then canonical min/max ball identity and segment identity
continuous_candidate_contract.stable_identity: ball pair, both domain segment identities, absolute TOI and event ordinal; recursive replay cannot apply the same contact twice
continuous_candidate_contract.same_toi_ambiguity: indistinguishable cross-domain ball contact versus table, pocket, departure, landing, return, or another contact fails the whole tick closed unless the existing island solver proves one deterministic simultaneous island
continuous_candidate_contract.initial_penetration: requires the existing unique-normal penetration policy; ambiguous penetration fails and rolls back

resolution_and_atomicity_contract.resolver: reuse existing rigid ball-ball contact mass, restitution, friction, normal/tangent impulse, contact arm, and tolerance conventions; do not invent a D6-only bounce constant
resolution_and_atomicity_contract.linear_and_angular_state: position, velocity, angularVelocity, rotationAxis, rotationAngle, speed, motionState, pocket state and physical domain are staged and committed together
resolution_and_atomicity_contract.angular_rule: airborne angular velocity is conserved before contact; the resolved contact may change angular state only by the existing contact impulse convention and may not reset or synthesize spin
resolution_and_atomicity_contract.momentum_and_energy: resolved pair obeys existing solver momentum, passive-energy, residual and finite-state tolerances
resolution_and_atomicity_contract.domain_rule: contact alone does not teleport either ball between physical domains; subsequent continuous table candidates decide landing, return, departure or pocket entry
resolution_and_atomicity_contract.failed_tick: restore the exact pre-tick GameState fields covered by the parent D6-A atomic contract and publish no partial private event list
resolution_and_atomicity_contract.private_only: candidate and resolution records remain physics-private D6-A data and are not appended to canonical PhysicsStepTelemetry, ShotFacts, rules outcomes, or product UI

required_tests_first_red_fixtures_exact.requirement: A descending or lateral airborne sphere strikes a moving cloth-supported sphere at a known analytic root; the observed absolute TOI and canonical pair identity match the independently computed root within the frozen solver tolerance.
An airborne sphere contacts a rail-top-supported sphere before either table feature; exact TOI, ordering, domain retention, and one stable identity are proven.
An airborne sphere contacts an outside-landing-supported sphere before floor contact; exact TOI, ordering, domain retention, and one stable identity are proven.

A nontrivial oblique cross-domain contact is compared with the existing rigid ball-ball resolver: normal/tangent impulse, post velocities, angular velocities, finite state, momentum and passive-energy bounds agree; pre-contact airborne spin is not reset.

A cross-domain contact followed by a landing or return in the same tick has strictly ordered absolute TOIs, unique identities, no duplicate contact, and whole-tick versus recursively split equivalence.

A constructed cross-domain ball contact indistinguishable from a table or pocket candidate either resolves through one existing deterministic simultaneous island or fails closed; the fixture requires the selected behavior and byte-exact transactional rollback on failure.
Separated, tangent-without-approach, and near-miss paths produce no contact identity or impulse and preserve the independent domain trajectories.
A high-speed path crosses the supported sphere between endpoints while start and end do not overlap; exactly one continuous contact is required. A mutation that checks only final overlap must fail.
The already-required mixed-domain cloth collision/surface telemetry and valid/invalid plane-observation controls remain byte/record equivalent; adding cross-domain candidates may not regress them.
Static and runtime audits prove no D6-B telemetry schema, ShotFacts, rules, UI, renderer, product, coordinate whitelist, new threshold, or consumer connection is introduced.

tests_first_and_implementation_sequence: Freeze an honest RED whose first cause is the absence of continuous cross-domain contact behavior, not a missing header or unrelated compile error.
Root and independent TA reproduce the RED and verify all ten fixtures are substantive before any production edit for this correction.
Implement the minimum continuous candidate, ordering, resolver reuse and atomic merge within the exact allowlist.
Run the dedicated tests at O0 and O2 with identical semantic output, then the parent D6-A focused target and broad headless physics regressions.
Freeze source/object/binary/command/stdout/stderr hashes and an implementation receipt; only then may Root consider D6-A CMake SOURCE_STABLE.
